why: It sits in the binary-search stage, but no search is needed. Whichever category you watch first, finishing it earlier can only help the second movie, so take the earliest finish r + d in that category. Then pick the second movie minimising max(t, r) + d. Try both category orders.
hints: You watch exactly two movies, one per category, one after the other. Try fixing which category goes first.
The second movie's finish max(t, release) + duration never gets worse when t gets smaller, so the first movie should be the one with the smallest release + duration.
For each order: t = min(r + d) over the first category, then min(max(t, r) + d) over the second. Answer is the better of the two orders. O(n + m).
pitfalls: Try both orders; comedy-first is not always best.
The second movie may start later than t if it has not been released yet: use max(t, r).
A movie can start exactly when the previous one ends.
constraints:
• 1 <= n, m <= 10^5
  • 1 <= comedyReleaseTime[i], comedyDuration[i], dramaReleaseTime[i], dramaDuration[i] <= 10^6
